research_rationale: Executive Order 12952 (February 24, 1995; 60 FR 11011) has one operative sentence: it amends Executive Order No. 12950 so that "the list of Labor Organizations" attached to that order includes "International Brotherhood of Firemen & Oilers". Executive Order 12950 (February 22, 1995) established an emergency board under section 9A of the Railway Labor Act. The amendment is a self-executing act that was complete when the President signed on February 24, 1995; the order contains no continuing command, standing rule or duty. The entry it inserted lives on only inside Executive Order 12950's list, so its further life belongs to that order and is recorded under savings. Searches of held texts for the number 12952 found only the order's own Federal Register text, the Federal Register daily-contents entry (fr-95-5129) and an APP transcription; no later instrument names it.
savings_reason: The inserted name became part of the list of labor organizations attached to Executive Order 12950 and is carried inside that order, not in Executive Order 12952. By its held Federal Register text Executive Order 12950 established an emergency board that was to report within 30 days of its creation on February 22, 1995 and to terminate on submission of that report, with the section 9A(c) status-quo period running 120 days from creation. No dossier evidence id holds the parent's end or the report date, so the parent's end is not asserted; the amendment's own command was spent on issue.
earlier_end_check: The held original is a single operative sentence with no condition or duration, and the order has no revival, delay or conditional effective date. The three bounded searches and the held-text search for the number 12952 located no earlier or later instrument that revokes, supersedes or amends it, so no earlier end competes with the date of signing.
scope_check: The order has one scope (the whole order is the one amendment of the list). No part of it was separately revoked or amended.
independent_command_check: The order has no command independent of the list amendment: no report, delegation, funding or continuing duty.
savings_check: The surviving effect is the inserted union name inside Executive Order 12950's list; it is carried by the parent and is stated under savings as transferred.

research_rationale: Executive Order 11125 (October 29, 1963; 28 FR 11609) delegated the President's authority under sections 205 and 208(b) of title 18, United States Code, to department and agency heads for certain presidential appointees. Section 703(b) of Executive Order 11222 (May 8, 1965; 30 FR 6469, held official Federal Register text) revokes it, and the same section says the revocation takes effect on the date the Civil Service Commission issues regulations under Section 701(a) of that order. The whole order is revoked, so no clause survives. The exact date of that issuance is not held in the packet, so each clause's first end is bounded (after May 8, 1965; the held 2005 notice FR Doc. 05-15927 says the first-listed regulation, 5 CFR part 735 subpart D, was effective October 1, 1965) but not fixed.

research_rationale: Executive Order 13593 (December 13, 2011; 76 FR 78451) amends Parts III and IV of the Manual for Courts-Martial, United States (prescribed by Executive Order 12473, as amended) as described in an Annex, and Sec. 2 provides that the amendments take effect 30 days from the date of the order, that is January 12, 2012. Its operative acts are self-executing amendments of the Manual: the order contains no continuing duty, reporting requirement or standing command, and Sec. 2(a) and (b) are rules of construction that protect conduct and proceedings begun before the effective date. The amended text continues as text of the Manual, which is a separate instrument, so the order's own commands were spent on its effective date, January 12, 2012. Searches of held texts for the number 13593 found only the order's own Federal Register text and later Federal Register documents that implement, cite or annotate it (2011-32486, 2012-25852, 2013-07804, 2016-06403, 2016-21874); none revokes, supersedes or amends it, and the Federal Register catalog note is empty, which does not by itself show current effect.
savings_reason: The amendments continue as text of the Manual for Courts-Martial, United States (prescribed by Executive Order 12473, as amended), which is a separate instrument; the surviving text is not a command of Executive Order 13593. Sec. 2(b) of the order also preserves proceedings begun before the effective date, which may proceed in the same manner and with the same effect as if the amendments had not been prescribed; that accrued protection attaches to those pre-effective-date matters.

research_rationale: Executive Order 13624 (August 30, 2012; 77 FR 54779) directs the Departments of Energy, Commerce and Agriculture and the Environmental Protection Agency, in coordination with named White House offices, to coordinate policies to encourage investment in industrial energy efficiency and combined heat and power (CHP), to engage stakeholders, and to take the listed supporting actions. The held Federal Register original was read in full. It has no sunset, expiry, termination condition or revocation; its only dates are the policy goal date of the end of 2020 in Sec. 2(a) and a 25 percent energy-intensity goal over 10 years, which describes an existing Department of Energy program in Sec. 2(c)(iv), not a limit on the order. The United States Code (release point 119-121, printed through 2026-10-09) prints the order in full as a note under 42 U.S.C. 6341 with no ending statement. A Department of Energy notice signed January 5, 2026 (91 FR 704, FR Doc. 2026-00153) still cites Executive Order 13624 as statutory authority for an information collection, which shows agency reliance but is not itself a legal predicate. The search of the held corpus for the order's number found only the order's own text and that notice, so no held later order amends, revokes or supersedes it; the Federal Register catalog note is empty, which does not establish current effect. The YES rests on the order's terms, the Code note and the absence of any held ending instrument.
savings_reason: No clause is terminated, so no ended command leaves a saved or accrued consequence; the bounded searches located no ending instrument and no saved or transferred function.
earlier_end_check: The held original has no duration, sunset or expiry; Sec. 3(b) (implementation "consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations") conditions how the order is carried out, not whether it continues. No held later instrument names the number 13624 other than a 2026 Department of Energy information-collection notice that cites it as authority. The bounded machine searches report no ending instrument.
scope_check: The order's scopes are the policy statement (Sec. 1), the Sec. 2 coordination directive with its paragraphs (a) to (d) and their subparagraphs, and the Sec. 3 general provisions. No partial revocation or amendment of any scope was located, so each is judged on the same evidence.
independent_command_check: Sec. 2(a), (b), (c) and (d) are separate directions to the agencies, but each is a continuing direction with no own end and no separate later event. Sec. 2(a) names the end of 2020 as the date by which the national goal is to be achieved; that date is the goal's target, not a stated end of the direction to coordinate and encourage, and no held source shows the direction stopped. Sec. 2(b) (public workshops) is a continuing direction whose performance is not shown by any held source.
savings_check: Nothing has ended, so there is no saving, transfer or accrual to carry.
